title: Resolve the exact compliance-stiffness boundary and arbitrarily small modal slack
statement: For the defined relative-CM response of any connected positive internal graph, C_CM*kappa_total>=1; positive caps are feasible iff Ccap*kappacap>=1. Equality forces one active pendant response. At normalized m=1,M=2,K=1,theta=1/2,Ccap=1/20, every kappacap>20 permits a finite positive two-branch improvement over the optimized pendant; at 20 none can improve and below 20 none is feasible. Every fixed finite spring cap has a positive gap above the severe-cap stiff-escape infimum, even at unbounded finite network order.

requires: Connected positive internal graph and normalized relative-CM force f_b=-1,f_j=m_j/(M-m)
Onset/escape-gap statements use the stated normalized thermal point and Ccap=1/20
provides: Topology-independent static feasibility and actual pendant sufficiency
Equality identifies active response while allowing dark modes
A legal small-mass split preserves compliance, pays stiffness and lowers the full Bose integral
Bounded fourth moment gives trace tails, so large network order cannot hide escape
assumptions: No vector, anharmonic, finite-contact, connector-mass, geometry/strain or measured-device transfer
No historical-priority or algorithmic advantage established; conventional designers receive the same synthesis information
Tiny positive slack gives existence, not uniform nonzero gain or a lower component-mass bound
The finite-cap gap is not a quantitative gap formula or a general attainment theorem
costs: One source split has stiffness 20+64*epsilon+O(epsilon^2) and a strictly negative objective derivative
The epsilon=1/10000 example costs about 20.0064001280 and saves about 5.48919e-8 in J; not optimal at that budget
Small slack can demand small masses and precision; no fabrication guarantee
contract.units: Compliance times total stiffness is dimensionless; onset examples use fixed source units
contract.obstruction: Distinguishes infeasible resources and true legal improvement from a failed dual or optimizer. No full-resource phase diagram follows.

evidence.range_scope: Exact graph-wide feasibility boundary and strict split improvement with arbitrarily small stiffness slack at the normalized source point.

evidence.quote: every fixed finite spring-sum cap has a strictly positive gap
evidence.range_scope: Static feasibility, legal splitting and bounded-stiffness obstruction to trace escape, including unbounded network order.

body: The static Cauchy/Rayleigh proof covers arbitrary graphs. A negative dual region is paired with an actual positive split and full-band expansion. Final L1 wording and rejected infeasible exploratory candidates are preserved.

review.scope: Actual completed audit is a separate version-bound overlay.
